name: Citation Metadata
description: Core information used to identify, describe, and cite a dataset.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: Person or organization responsible for creating the dataset.
fields.description: The full name of a person or organization credited with creating the dataset. Enter names in the form preferred for citation.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.summary: Persistent identifier associated with the author.
fields.description: A globally unique identifier for the named author, such as an ORCID iD. Use the corresponding scheme in Identifier Scheme.

fields.name: Identifier Scheme
fields.summary: Scheme used for the author identifier.
fields.description: The controlled vocabulary value that identifies which system issued or manages the author identifier.

fields.name: Other Identifier
fields.summary: Identifier assigned to the dataset by another system.
fields.description: An identifier other than the repository's primary persistent identifier. Pair it with the organization recorded in Other Identifier Agency.

fields.name: Other Identifier Agency
fields.summary: Organization that issued the other identifier.
fields.description: The name of the agency, archive, or registration service responsible for assigning the related other identifier.

name: Geospatial Metadata
description: Spatial coverage and geographic boundaries associated with a dataset.

fields.name: Geographic Coverage
fields.summary: Place or region represented by the dataset.
fields.description: A named geographic area covered by the data, ranging from a specific locality to a country or larger region.

fields.name: Westernmost Longitude
fields.summary: Western edge of the dataset's bounding box.
fields.description: The westernmost longitude in decimal degrees. West longitudes use negative values.

fields.name: Easternmost Longitude
fields.summary: Eastern edge of the dataset's bounding box.
fields.description: The easternmost longitude in decimal degrees. West longitudes use negative values.

name: Social Science Metadata
description: Study design and population concepts used in social science research.

fields.name: Unit of Analysis
fields.summary: Basic entity examined by the study.
fields.description: The type of entity about which observations are recorded, such as an individual, household, event, or organization.

fields.name: Universe
fields.summary: Population to which the study applies.
fields.description: A description of the population, objects, or events that the study intends to represent.
fields.example: Adults living in the United States

fields.name: Time Method
fields.summary: Temporal structure used by the study.
fields.description: The study's relationship to time, such as cross-sectional, longitudinal, or repeated cross-sectional.

name: Astronomy Metadata
description: Observational targets and equipment used to collect astronomy data.

fields.name: Object
fields.summary: Celestial object targeted by the observation.
fields.description: The common name, catalog designation, or other identifier of the astronomical target.

fields.name: Telescope
fields.summary: Telescope used to collect the observation.
fields.description: The telescope or observatory facility responsible for gathering the source measurements.

fields.name: Instrument
fields.summary: Instrument attached to the observing system.
fields.description: The detector, camera, spectrograph, or other instrument used to record the observation.
